name: Efficiency security tradeoff

subjectOf.text: Misestimating the hot money ratio fails in both directions: overestimation makes the currency more costly to use, and underestimation leaves it insecure, so efficiency and security are in direct tension.
subjectOf.abstract: A currency that overestimates this hot money ratio will cost more to use. A currency that underestimates the ratio will be insecure
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Vadhindran K. Rao, Stable Cryptocurrencies - First Order Principles (2019). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3402701

subjectOf.text: Determining what fraction of a currency is hot money is necessary for efficiently defending its stability: overestimating the hot money ratio makes the currency costlier to use, and underestimating it makes the currency insecure.
subjectOf.abstract: Therefore, determining the fraction of a currency that is hot money is necessary for efficient defense of its stability. A currency that overestimates this hot money ratio will cost more to use. A currency that underestimates the ratio will be insecure.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Finance (DeFi) (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3782216
